% generated by experiments/e2_dependence.py
Rejection rates at $\alpha=0.05$ with Wilson 95\% intervals; $N$ = valid replications under $H_0$ / per alternative (minimum); independent windows. Family (a): a fraction $\delta$ of the $Q$ windows has $L$ independent returns; family (b): $Q$ windows are concatenations of independent $P$ blocks of length $b$. Every return of $Q$ has exactly the marginal law of $P$.
$p$-values: permutation of the held-out evaluation labels with the network fixed (W-critic, LR-critic, C2ST; exact for independent windows), permutation (MMD, Sig-MMD), asymptotic (KS), Monte Carlo with 4000 null values ($n=500$), 1000 null values ($n=2000$) and randomised ties (LR oracle).
$^{\dagger}$ Every return of $Q$ has exactly the marginal law of $P$, so KS (pooled returns, marginal only) has no power by construction; the returns of one GARCH window share the conditional variance, so its nominal $p$-value is not valid either (rejection rate under $H_0$ at nominal 5\%: mix, $n=500$: 0.065 [0.038, 0.108]; mix, $n=2000$: 0.090 [0.058, 0.138]; block, $n=500$: 0.095 [0.062, 0.144]; block, $n=2000$: 0.075 [0.046, 0.120]). Its rejection rates are size distortions, not power.
The LR oracle is approximate (Monte Carlo): the $P$ window and block densities integrate the conditional variance at the window or block start over $K=512$ draws of its law, the position marginals over $K_m=2048$ draws; statistic and null use the same draws, so the oracle test is exact but only approximately most powerful (not a strict power bound).
Marginal check (two-sample KS between independent returns of $P$, one per window, and of $Q$ at the i.i.d.-marginal level): mix $\delta$$\,=\,$1: $D=0.0027$, $p=0.00$ (1000000 vs 1000000 returns); block $b$$\,=\,$1: $D=0.0011$, $p=0.62$ (1000000 vs 1000000 returns).
